transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-05 16:00 UTC · 52 minutes · Recording available
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Luis (Redwood SE), Hannah (CSM), Daniel (CTO, Cobalt), Priya (SRE), Liam (Data Eng)

Summary: Quick kickoff/handoff from Sales to CS/SE for Cobalt Analytics pilot. Discussed deployment options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), network constraints, KMS/H-S-M, SOC2 questions, success criteria for pilot, timeline and next steps.

00:00 Maya: alright good afternoon everyone, uh thanks for joining. quick intros then we'll jump into what success looks like and the technical bits.
00:12 Daniel: hey all, Daniel here - CTO at Cobalt. we're building an analyst-facing insights layer, lots of PII-ish logs, so security and residency matter.
00:20 Maya: great, thanks Daniel. Priya?
00:22 Priya: Priya, SRE. we'll handle infra and networking, i've got questions about egress and whether we need full VPC peering.
00:30 Luis: hi all, Luis from Redwood infra team. i'll run through the deployment options; i know you hit us up about on-prem-ish constraints.
00:40 Liam: liam, data eng, i'll own the integration with our event pipeline and batch scoring.
00:48 Hannah: hannah, customer success. i'll be your day-to-day for the pilot run.
01:00 Maya: cool. quick agenda: alignment on pilot goals, discuss network and security constraints, recommend deployment mode and config, and agree next steps.
01:10 Daniel: on goals — we want to validate latency under realistic loads for our interactive analyst UI, and confirm that sensitive rows never leave the VPC. plus a short cost estimate for 6 months.
01:25 Luis: noted. two high-level paths: 1) Hosted Redwood API — fastest time to value, no infra for you but you'd send data to our hosted endpoints (obviously not ideal for sensitive data unless tokenization/masking is done), 2) Redwood Dedicated — reserved GPU capacity in your cloud account with VPC peering and private routing, 3) Redwood Private — customer-managed control plane (VPC or on-prem) for full isolation.
01:52 Priya: okay quick stop — when you say "VPC peering" do you mean we need peering or can we use egress via NAT gateway? our security team prefers peering but there's a procurement overhead.
02:05 Luis: good question. we support both patterns. peering gives lower latency and tighter isolation, NAT is possible but means egress to Redwood's IPs and requires TLS + mTLS options. either way, we can work through firewall rules.
02:20 Daniel: and KMS? we need customer-managed keys.
02:24 Luis: yes, Redwood Private supports your K-M-S and H-S-M integrations. Dedicated supports BYOK for encryption at rest; hosted has platform-managed KMS only.
02:34 Liam: curious about KV cache — can we keep KV cache local to our VPC so that embeddings and cached responses don't hit multi-tenant storage?
02:43 Luis: the runtime supports prefix and KV caching; on Dedicated/Private you can keep the cache in your network/local redis. on hosted it's shared and encrypted.
02:55 Priya: how about SOC2? we'll need audit logs and retention info for compliance.
03:00 Hannah: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II (we'll attach certs), we also provide audit log exports and can maintain a separate retention policy for your tenant on Dedicated/Private.
03:12 Daniel: timeline — we're aiming for a pilot with a small cohort by mid-November, production in early January if things look good. is that feasible?
03:20 Maya: yes, realistic. pilot needs: runbook + onboarding checklist, network diagrams, shared test prompts and evals, and a perf matrix. we can do pilot kick-off week of Nov 15.
03:32 Priya: perf matrix — we need latency p95 and throughput at 1k concurrent sessions. can you recommend batching configs and model quantization?
03:42 Luis: definitely. for interactive UI we usually recommend low-latency configs: small batch sizes, dynamic batching, and 4-bit quant on certain open models for Dedicated. i'll put numbers in the perf spreadsheet. there might be accuracy tradeoffs; we'll flag evals.
03:58 Liam: integration specifics — we have a Kafka-based pipeline. is there a typical adapter or do we push via REST?
04:06 Luis: both are possible. many customers use an intermediation layer: Kafka -> microservice -> Redwood REST or SDK. we can provide SDK examples in Node/Python. for high throughput, batching at the service layer reduces token cost.
04:20 Daniel: any gotchas for our cloud provider? we run in us-east-1 with standard security posture.
04:25 Luis: we have infra in us-east-1; Dedicated instances are available there. for Private, if you want an on-prem appliance that's more scheduling, but VPC private control plane is the common pattern.
04:38 Priya: firewall rules — what's the egress IP list? we need that for our firewall team to sign off.
04:44 Maya: we'll attach the CIDR and FQDN list in the runbook. action item: Maya to include exact egress IPs and sample security policy.
04:53 Hannah: also i'll send the onboarding cadence — two weekly 30-minute checkpoints during pilot and a triage channel.
05:00 Daniel: sounds good. now on success criteria — besides latency and residency, we want failure modes defined: if a model falls below quality thresholds, auto-fallback to a smaller model, and clear logging for mispredictions.
05:15 Luis: yes, Redwood supports automatic fallback policies, route-based rollouts and per-route tracing. we'll include config examples. logging is exportable to your syslog/SIEM.
05:26 Liam: will we get token-level cost breakdowns?
05:29 Hannah: yes, console has token-level cost and latency breakdown; we'll give you sample dashboards and an export hook into your billing system.
05:38 Daniel: procurement questions — what about a short-term Dedicated commit for the pilot? we don't want a long contract until we're validating.
05:46 Maya: we can do a month-to-month reserved pool with optional burst; the commercial will propose an introductory pilot pricing. Luis will add the cost model for the pilot.
05:55 Priya: okay network constraints again — we use an egress proxy that rewrites TLS SNI in some cases, is that supported?
06:03 Luis: we have seen proxies that terminate TLS; if it mutates headers we need to test. recommend staging network tests.
06:10 Daniel: questions from my security team: can you provide an on-site audit or remote pen-test report?
06:15 Hannah: we can share our pen test summary and SOC2 report. for an on-site audit we'll coordinate via our security team and exec sponsor.
06:24 Maya: quick recap and next steps: we'll send runbook, egress IPs, perf matrix, and a proposed pilot pricing. Priya will provide networking details. Luis will prepare a Dedicated vs Hosted technical note. Hannah will set cadence.
06:40 Priya: thanks — i'll try to get the firewall list and any proxy configs by Monday.
06:45 Liam: and i'll assemble test prompts and the dataset subset (anonymized) for the evals.
06:50 Daniel: ok let's target 2026-11-15 for pilot kick-off; please send invites.
06:55 Maya: will do. any final questions?
07:00 Daniel: none from me. thanks everyone.
07:05 Hannah: i'll follow up with calendar invites and the runbook link.
07:10 Maya: thanks all, meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcript: occasional mis-hearings present (e.g., KMS transcribed as K-M-S; HSM as H-S-M), some interruptions. Links referenced: onboarding runbook (link: https://redwood.example/runbooks/cobalt-onboarding), SOC2 cert (link: https://redwood.example/security/soc2), perf spreadsheet placeholder (link: https://redwood.example/perf/cobalt-pilot).

End of transcript.
